body:
Arguably we can say that something is wrong with our choice. We mixed up the `__` and `--` and that made a divergence from the classic [two dashes style naming convention variant](https://en.bem.info/methodology/naming-convention/#two-dashes-style).

However, reading the convention from the beginning of the article, we can argue that the syntax doesn't really matter as long as the Block Element Modifier pattern is used while naming the css classes. And that's what is implemented in the current state of the css file that we provide.

Also we can see that if we wanted to go for purity we should use the underscore syntax, which is the one advertise from the [start of the article](https://en.bem.info/methodology/naming-convention/#naming-convention) and that we can [see in action](https://en.bem.info/methodology/naming-convention/#example-of-using-the-naming-convention) in the example section.

I think it boils down to letting the user choose the convention, no?
